<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard packaging variables such as pkgname, pkgver, source, and sha256sums, all of which are static and use straightforward string expansions. The only dynamic element is the `_release` variable, which constructs a URL using the pkgver value. This is a common and safe practice in AUR PKGBUILDs to avoid repetition in source URLs.

There are no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements in the global scope. The `source` array and `sha256sums` use static, inline values or simple variable expansions that do not involve command execution. Notably, no `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or other potentially dangerous operations occur at parse time.

Since `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources the PKGBUILD without executing any of the package functions (`package_ttf-furifont-hiragana`, etc.), and there is no evidence of malicious code executing during sourcing, this file is safe for this stage.
</details>

No executable code, build scripts, or install hooks are present in this file. The content is purely declarative metadata used by the AUR build system. As such, there is no evidence of malicious behavior, data exfiltration, or supply-chain attacks.

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard AUR package for distributing Japanese variable fonts (Furifont) with furigana support. It fetches prebuilt font files and license texts from the official GitHub releases of the upstream project (antfu/furifont), which is consistent with expected packaging practices. The sources are pinned to a specific version (v0.6.1) and include proper checksums (sha256sums) for all downloaded files, ensuring integrity.

The build process consists solely of installing the pre-downloaded TTF font files and license metadata into appropriate system directories under `$pkgdir`. There are no network operations, dynamic downloads, or executions during the build or install phases. The package splits into two subpackages (`ttf-furifont-hiragana` and `ttf-furifont-romaji`), each installing its respective font files and sharing the same license files. All operations are transparent and limited to font installation.

No obfuscated code, dangerous commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`), or unexpected system modifications are present. The URLs used are legitimate and match the project's stated homepage. The package follows standard AUR packaging guidelines and poses no evidence of supply-chain compromise or malicious behavior.
</details>
